info.name: Tasks API
info.description:
Task assignment and tracking.

Every route is open to any authenticated member of the company, because being a head of department is not a role — an HOD is whoever departments.head_employee_id points at, and they may hold any user_companies.role. The real authorization runs in service/Task/taskAccessService.js against the actual employee and department records.

Plan gate: tasks.manage (reads stay open when a plan lapses).

request.description:
Assign work to an employee.

Who may call it: an admin (any employee in the company) or a head of department (only employees in the department they head — departments.head_employee_id). Anyone else gets 403.

due_at without an offset is read in the company's timezone, so '2026-08-25T17:00' means 5 PM where the work happens. department_id is NOT accepted — it is frozen from the assignee's record, because it is both the HOD permission boundary and the dashboard's grouping key.

{
    "title": "Fix the payslip export",
    "description": "PDF renders blank for December",
    "category_id": "{{category_id}}",
    "assigned_to_employee_id": "{{employee_id}}",
    "priority": "urgent",
    "due_at": "2026-08-25T17:00",
    "due_timezone": "Asia/Dubai",
    "watcher_employee_ids": []
}

request.description: Counters for whatever the caller is allowed to see — the board header. `overdue` counts live tasks whose deadline has passed, not a status.

The task with its full transition history, remarks and watchers.

`allowed_transitions` is what THIS caller may move it to right now — render the status dropdown from it and a rule change never needs a client release. An employee looking at a submitted task sees [] there: only a manager signs work off.

A task the caller may not see returns 404, not 403 — telling someone a task exists but is none of their business leaks who is working on what.

request.description:
The terms of the task: title, description, category, criticality, deadline, assignee.

Deliberately NOT open to the assignee, even on their own task — if the person doing the work can move their own deadline, every on-time figure on the performance dashboard is self-reported.

Passing assigned_to_employee_id reassigns: the frozen department_id follows the new assignee, they join the watcher list, and they get a 'reassigned to you' notification. Send due_at: null to clear a deadline.

request.description:
The status machine. open → in_progress → submitted → completed, with reopened and cancelled off to the side.

The assignee may move their own work to in_progress, submitted or back to open. They may NOT mark it completed — that is the manager's sign-off — and may not cancel it. Admins and HODs may make any transition the machine allows.

Every call writes a task_status_history row in the same transaction, and freezes whether the deadline had already passed. That log is what the performance dashboard is built from.
